name: Pixelcasso
soft_passes: #2 subject mass sits left-of-centre, not on the optical grid
#4 face reads at 16px but the pixel-dissolve concept smears into generic low-res photo
#8 coherent but one flat art plane, none of the era's stacked-plane depth
failures: #3 no nameable solid silhouette — filled black it is just a square with a face-void
#10 single dark raster wholly colour-dependent; mono/clear/tinted renders would destroy it, no layered/vector source
#12 no text but a raster reproduction of an external oil painting — the photographic/non-vector element HIG warns against

palette.background: flat gallery-black #030608 warming to #1A150C at lower edge

light_model: painterly frontal/upper-left portrait light on the face against near-black; matte, no specular, no baked macOS micro-shadow — internally consistent but not the top-down macOS model
layer_stack: oil-painted profile portrait (floral crown, rosy cheek, gold hair)
devices: pixel-dissolve pun (classical portrait quantizing into mosaic blocks = Pixel + Picasso)
full-bleed art reproduction as the icon, no glyph/chrome/tool overlay
gallery-black ground making the pale portrait glow
rhymes_hint: full-bleed scene / photo-hero icons (photo-editor family, image-in-squircle strategy) and concept-pun icons whose payload is wordplay rather than a tool metaphor
notes: Source is a 192x192 web render, not the 1024 master — mask edge, corner clipping and sub-pixel shadows unassessable; block sizes read at 192px scale. Brand-coherence gap: cover is navy #132238 + steel/cream gradient + serif 'P' monogram; icon shares none of that palette (near-black + gold + skin, no navy, no monogram) — App-Store face and wordmark diverge. Originality/licensing flag: portrait reads as an actual or closely-imitated Picasso painting; shipping a famous artist's work as an icon is a rights risk. Era does not quote any macOS era; classified custom (art-reproduction + digital dissolve).
